newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs looking "toppish", dealers say.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs looking "toppish", dealers say.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended generally firmer on Monday but dealers said both were looking "toppish" and could slide back soon.
The two markets opened sharply firmer on the back of an unexpected dip in U.S. payrolls data on Friday.
The benchmark March Euroyen hit a contract high of 99.36 in early trade with gains seen in all forward contracts.
But the market then fell sharply on comments by the head of publicity at Japan's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).

The LDP official was reported by a U.S. news agency as saying that a Japanese interest rate hike, including a rise in the official discount rate, might be considered after the general election on October 20.
"The big effect was on JGBs, which tumbled from a high of 123.44 all the way down to 122.95 before steadying," said a Singapore-based trader.
Dealers said Monday's fall had been a useful reminder to the market of how long the current rally had continued without a correction.
"I think we're getting quite tired on JGBs," said a dealer.
"Yields are now too low, RSIs (relative strength indices) are showing the market as overbought and it's hard to attract new interest at these levels."
"These kind of levels reflect unrealistic expectations of low interest rates staying with us...As soon as that is realised the market must come off," he said.
Another dealer said he thought the back-months of the Euroyen futures on SIMEX could fall by at least 20 points.
March Euroyen ended at 99.31 against its IMM close at 99.34. June closed at 99.17 against 99.22.
December JGBs were last traded at 123.06 against their opening level of 123.28.
Eurodollar futures finished higher in reaction to Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report.
"The U.S. euphoria was retained during Singapore hours, but it didn't add to it," said a dealer.
The March Eurodollar contract closed at 94.30, slightly below its IMM settlement at 94.33.
